title: Localized derived unit represented by the closed-test section chain
statement: For the coefficient ring, affine closed-fibre square, w-contractible test and supplied K-injective representatives of [def-sfb-closed-test-kinjective-section-maps], the explicit actual section-unit chain followed by j, under localizationModel and the final-object section identity, equals the derived restriction of [def-sfb-closed-test-derived-exchange-maps] followed by the inverse canonical pullback-composition comparison.

source.place: Tag 09BL, lemma-closed-immersion-affines-apply; derived.tex Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors, and sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; agent unit–counit calculation, returned proof steps 5–7.

proof.text: Write $I_T=\mathcal I|_T$ and $J_0=\mathcal J|_{T_0}$. Work on the localized section-ring sites through the equivalences of step 1. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized-universes], $I_T$ and $J_0$ are K-injective; localization is restriction of sections as in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The normalized pullback identification of [lem-sfb-closed-test-kinjective-section-models] turns $j|_{T_0}$ into a quasi-isomorphism $j_0:a^*I_T\to J_0$. Apply [lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization] now to $a^*\dashv a_*$. The adjunct of $j_0$ is $a_*j_0\circ\eta_{a,I_T}$. Since $Q(j_0)$ identifies its target with $a^*QI_T$, the localized class of this adjunct represents the actual derived unit $QI_T\to Ra_*a^*QI_T$. This proves the required normalization for the unit even though $a^*I_T$ need not be K-injective.

source.place: Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; derived.tex Tag 09T5 for the normalized derived adjunct.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], $a_*J_0$ is K-injective because $a^*$ is exact. Therefore $R\Gamma(T,-)$ on the unit of step 5 is computed by the actual chain map $\Gamma(T,I_T)\to\Gamma(T,a_*J_0)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $a$ followed by the map to the point with coefficient ring $\Gamma(T,\Lambda_T)$. Its representative normalization permits the identity resolution of $a_*J_0$, so the derived composition comparison is precisely the degreewise identity $\Gamma(T,a_*J_0)=\Gamma(T_0,J_0)$. Forgetting the section-ring action gives the asserted comparison in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$. On sections the map from step 5 is $j(T_0)\circ\eta_a$, which is the map of step 4; hence that map is exactly the derived restriction with the stated normalization.

theorem closed_test_chain_unit_normalization
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (a : Ideal A)
    {X XZ : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    (h : XZ ⟶ X) (fZ : XZ ⟶ Spec (.of (A ⧸ a)))
    (w : IsPullback h fZ f (closedMap A a))
    (V : (Spec (.of (A ⧸ a))).AffineProEt)
    [IsWContractibleRing Γ(V.left, ⊤)]
    [IsWContractibleRing Γ((liftedTest A a V).left, ⊤)]
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus
      (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X)))
    (L : CochainComplex
      (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X)) ℤ)
    [L.IsKInjective] (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅ K.obj)
    (J : CochainComplex
      (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology XZ) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ XZ)) ℤ)
    [J.IsKInjective] (j : (complexes (CondensedRing.upperStar Λ h)).obj L ⟶ J)
    [QuasiIso j] :
    HEq (DerivedCategory.Q.map (sectionChain Λ A a w V L J j) ≫
        globalLocalizationModel Λ (testFibre fZ (closedTest A a V))
          ((CondensedRing.upperStar Λ h).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj)
          J (pullRepresentative Λ h K.obj L e J j))
      (globalLocalizationModel Λ (testFibre f (liftedTest A a V)) K.obj L e ≫
        (ClosedTestDerivedExchangeModel.restriction Λ (testArrow A a w V)).app
          ((CondensedRing.upperStar Λ
            (testFibre f (liftedTest A a V)).hom).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj) ≫
        (condensedModuleSections Λ
          (testFibre fZ (closedTest A a V)).left).rightDerivedFunctor.map
            ((derivedTestPullbackComposition Λ A a w V).inv.app K.obj))
